en: Liquid water expands by approximately nine percent in volume when it freezes into solid ice.
Seawater contains about 35 grams of dissolved salts per liter, making it a highly concentrated solution.
Osmium is the densest naturally occurring element, weighing about 22.59 grams per cubic centimeter, twice as dense as lead.
A standard empty aluminum soda can weighs only 15 grams, making it about 30 times lighter than a glass bottle.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, requiring 3,422 degrees Celsius to change from solid to liquid.
Milk is a colloid where tiny fat globules, measuring about two to five micrometers across, are suspended in water.
At room temperature, oxygen gas molecules move at an average speed of roughly 480 meters per second, faster than a jet.
Helium has the lowest boiling point of any element, turning from a liquid to a gas at minus 268.9 degrees Celsius.
Spider silk is a natural polymer that is five times stronger than steel of the exact same weight and thickness.
Brass is a solid metal mixture typically containing about 67 percent copper and 33 percent zinc.
A typical wood campfire burns at around 600 degrees Celsius, which is hot enough to melt solid lead.
Diamond is the hardest natural material on Earth, scoring a perfect 10 on the Mohs hardness scale.
